root_cause.sql_injection: User-controlled input is concatenated directly into a SQL statement instead of being passed as a bound parameter.
root_cause.sql_injection2: A SQL string is built by string concatenation, so any attacker-controlled value becomes part of the query grammar itself.
root_cause.hardcoded_secret: A credential is embedded as a literal in source code, so it ships with every copy of the codebase and every commit in version history.
root_cause.command_injection: A shell command is constructed from data that can be influenced by a caller/user, and the shell is invoked to interpret it.
root_cause.insecure_deserialization: Untrusted bytes are deserialized with a format (pickle/unsafe YAML/native object streams) that can execute arbitrary code during deserialization.
root_cause.eval_exec: Dynamic code evaluation is applied to a value whose origin is not guaranteed to be a trusted, literal expression.
root_cause.weak_crypto: A cryptographically broken or deprecated primitive is used for a security-sensitive operation.
root_cause.xss: Output containing potentially attacker-influenced content is written into an HTML response without escaping.
root_cause.debug_mode: Debug mode is left enabled, which is intended for local development, not production traffic.
root_cause.path_traversal: A filesystem path is built from request input without normalizing/validating it against an allowed base directory.
root_cause.ssrf: The application makes arbitrary outbound requests to addresses derived from unvalidated user input.

best_practice.sql_injection: Always use parameterized queries or an ORM query builder; never format user input into SQL text.
best_practice.sql_injection2: Treat every user-supplied value as data, never as part of the query string.
best_practice.hardcoded_secret: Store secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager, and rotate any secret that was ever committed.
best_practice.command_injection: Prefer library APIs over shelling out; if a shell command is unavoidable, pass an argument list and never `shell=True` with untrusted input.
best_practice.insecure_deserialization: Use JSON (or another data-only format) for untrusted input, and never unpickle data you did not create yourself.
best_practice.eval_exec: Avoid eval/exec entirely for anything derived from user input; use ast.literal_eval or a real parser instead.
best_practice.weak_crypto: Use SHA-256 or better for integrity, and bcrypt/Argon2/scrypt (never a bare hash) for password storage.
best_practice.xss: Rely on your templating engine's autoescaping and set output via textContent, not innerHTML.
best_practice.debug_mode: Gate debug mode behind an environment variable that defaults to false, and never enable it in a deployed environment.
best_practice.path_traversal: Resolve the final path and assert it is still inside the intended base directory before opening it.
best_practice.ssrf: Implement strict allow-listing of domains and IP protocols before issuing server-side HTTP calls.

bug_root_cause.bare except: The exception type is not specified, so the handler intercepts every exception — including ones it wasn't written to handle.
bug_root_cause.empty catch: The exception is caught but never logged or handled, so failures are silently discarded.
bug_root_cause.mutable default: A list/dict default argument is created once at function-definition time and then shared across every call that doesn't pass its own value.
bug_root_cause.too many parameters: The function accepts many independent parameters instead of a single cohesive object, which is a sign it is doing too much or its inputs aren't modeled.
bug_root_cause.deep nesting: Conditional logic is nested many levels deep instead of using early returns/guard clauses, making the control flow hard to follow and test.
bug_root_cause.long function: The function accumulates multiple responsibilities instead of delegating to smaller, named helpers.
bug_root_cause.long method: The method accumulates multiple responsibilities instead of delegating to smaller, named helpers.
bug_root_cause.global: Mutable global state introduces hidden coupling between disparate functions.
bug_root_cause.unclosed: Resources (files, sockets) may leak if exceptions occur before explicit close calls.

bug_best_practice.bare except: Catch the specific exception type you expect and handle or log it explicitly.
bug_best_practice.empty catch: Always log or otherwise act on a caught exception; never leave a catch block empty.
bug_best_practice.mutable default: Default mutable arguments to None and construct the object inside the function body.
bug_best_practice.too many parameters: Group related parameters into a dataclass/struct so the function signature documents intent.
bug_best_practice.deep nesting: Return early on invalid/edge cases so the main logic isn't nested inside multiple conditionals.
bug_best_practice.long function: Keep functions focused on one responsibility; extract helpers for reuse and testability.
bug_best_practice.long method: Keep methods focused on one responsibility; extract helpers for reuse and testability.
bug_best_practice.global: Pass dependencies explicitly to functions or encapsulate state inside classes.
bug_best_practice.unclosed: Use context managers (`with` statements or try-with-resources) for deterministic cleanup.
